item.title: Switzerland harmonizes the 2026 UN sanctions ordinances
item.description: On 25 September 2026, the Federal Council decided to harmonise four sanctions ordinances, extending the exemption from notification and authorisation for certain Iranian transactions to international organisations.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Federal Council decides on 25 September 2026 - Four harmonized ordinances on financial measures - Iranian exemption extended to international organizations
## Key facts - Date → 25 September 2026 - Previous action → 13 August 2025 - Basis → UN sanctions - Ordinances → North Korea, Iran, ISIL (Da'esh), Al-Qaeda and Taliban - Exemption → certain transactions of international organizations
On 25 September 2026, in Bern, the Federal Council decided to standardize and clarify the financial provisions contained in four ordinances implementing UN sanctions relating to terrorist financing and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction. This is the core of the press release published on the same date.
### Four ordinances, one coordinated action
The texts concerned relate to the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, the Islamic Republic of Iran, persons, groups, companies and entities linked to the organizations ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaeda, as well as persons and groups linked to the Taliban. The four ordinances implement, in particular, the sanctions of the United Nations Security Council on terrorist financing and the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.
The Federal Council explains that the amendments correspond to the clarifications and harmonizations made on 13 August 2025 in the respective ordinances. Those amendments were based on European Union sanctions. With the legislative act of 25 September 2026, attention is now focused on financial measures based on resolutions of the United Nations Security Council. The press release therefore presents the new action as a targeted harmonization of the financial provisions, with an explicit reference to the UN sanctions framework.
### The exemption for the ordinance on Iran
There is also a specific provision for the ordinance establishing measures against the Islamic Republic of Iran. From now on, international organizations will benefit from an exemption from notification and authorization obligations for certain transactions. The exemptions from the same obligations for transfers of assets provided for by the ordinance have been extended to these organizations.
The source speaks of certain transactions and does not formulate the exemption as referring indiscriminately to all operations connected with Iran. The publication also includes the PDF entitled Ordinance concerning the amendment of ordinances on sanctions in relation to proliferation and terrorist financing. The topic should be kept distinct from the information on [conti bancari in Svizzera](nav:banks): here the document concerns the financial rules governing sanctions. ## What changes operationally
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the amendment should be read as a scope rule. The press release focuses the intervention on the wording of the financial provisions contained in the four ordinances and on the precise scope of the Iranian exemptions. The practical point is to understand which text applies and which transaction is being examined.
### The distinction guiding the review
The first element is the basis of the measure. The clarifications of 13 August 2025 were linked to European Union sanctions; the act of 25 September 2026 emphasizes financial measures based on resolutions of the United Nations Security Council. These are two references that must be kept distinct when reading the press release: the latter is what the Federal Council identifies as the focus of the new legislative act.
| Profile | Reference cited | Effect described | | --- | --- | --- | | Previous intervention | 13 August 2025 and European Union sanctions | Clarifications and harmonizations in the respective ordinances | | Act of 25 September 2026 | Resolutions of the United Nations Security Council | Emphasis on financial measures based on UN sanctions | | Ordinance on Iran | Transfers of assets | Exemptions from notification and authorization obligations extended to international organizations for certain transactions |
The second element concerns the relationship between the entity and the transaction. For an international organization, the matter cannot be resolved by merely belonging to the category: the transaction must be linked to the Ordinance on Iran and to the specific transactions for which the exemption is provided. The same extension is not described for the other three ordinances. This is the practical boundary that prevents automatically transferring the Iranian exemption to every financial measure concerning sanctions.
For anyone consulting a [dichiarazione delle imposte](nav:tax-return), the connection is purely editorial: the press release does not address ordinary taxation, but notification and authorization obligations within sanctions ordinances. The correct reading starts with the subject matter and the applicable text, not with a comparison to different tax procedures.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## How to check a transaction
The amendment can be translated into a sequence of documentary checks, without replacing the titles of the ordinances with a generic category of sanctions. The objective is to keep the applicable text, the basis of the measure and any exemption separate.
### Five steps
1. Identify the relevant ordinance. Verify whether the reference is the Democratic People's Republic of Korea, the Islamic Republic of Iran, persons, groups, undertakings and entities linked to the ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaeda organizations, or persons and groups linked to the Taliban.
2. Classify the basis of the financial provision. The communication distinguishes the clarifications and harmonizations of 13 August 2025, based on European Union sanctions, from the focus now placed on measures based on resolutions of the United Nations Security Council.
3. If the ordinance is the one on Iran, identify the subject involved. The exemption indicated by the Federal Council extends to international organizations; this element must be considered together with the type of transaction.
4. Check the obligation concerned. The verification must concern precisely the notification, authorization or transfer of assets, because the communication links the exemption to certain transactions and to the exemptions provided for by the ordinance.
5. Compare the result with the published text. The SECO page reports the PDF entitled Ordinance concerning the amendment of ordinances on sanctions in relation to proliferation and terrorist financing. It is the reference to use to avoid confusing the harmonization of provisions with an unlimited exemption.
This sequence is also useful when the question comes from an organization that has to examine a transaction connected to Iran: first the text is identified, then the category of the subject is verified, and finally the operation and obligation are checked. If one of these steps remains unclear, it is not possible to derive from the communication alone a broader exemption than the one indicated.

item.title: Swiss franc decline: signals to watch through November
item.description: The Swiss franc has fallen about 5% from its spring 2026 highs, equal to the decline in 2023 and less than >6% in 2024; the seasonal window runs from late September to early November.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The franc has lost about 5% from the highs of spring 2026 - In 2023, the decline had reached similar levels - In 2024, the correction had exceeded 6% - The seasonal window runs from late September to early November
## Key facts - Comparison period → last five years - Peak → spring 2026 - Franc's loss → about 5% against the euro - 2024 correction → over 6% - Seasonal window → late September-early November
From the highs reached in the first part of 2026, the Swiss franc has lost ground against the euro. After months of weakness, the Swiss currency faces a precise question: can the decline continue, or is the market approaching a turning point?
For those working in Switzerland and regularly converting their salary into euros, the movement has a direct effect on the amount received in the single currency. When the franc is weaker, the same salary yields fewer euros. The [comparatore CHF/EUR](nav:exchange) makes it possible to track the relationship between the two currencies, keeping the observed data distinct from the hypothesis about the future.
### A loss already seen in recent years
The analysis of the declines recorded by the franc over the last five years measures the currency's distance from previous highs. The movement that began after the peak of spring 2026 has led to a loss of about 5% against the euro.
The figure is not presented as exceptional in historical terms. In 2023, the decline had reached similar levels; in 2024, however, the correction had exceeded 6%. The comparison serves to place the current fluctuation within a sequence of movements already observed, without automatically turning it into a forecast.
The figure becomes interesting precisely because the franc is in an area where, in recent years, several periods of weakness have begun to lose momentum. The wording remains cautious: this does not mean that the low has already been reached, but it indicates that a significant part of the downward movement may be behind us.
A second signal comes from the seasonality of the exchange rate between the Swiss franc and the euro. The analysis conducted with Forecaster on the average behavior of the last ten years highlights a particular dynamic between the end of September and the beginning of November. The source identifies that window, together with statistical signals and institutional investors' positioning, as a period to monitor in the coming weeks. No certain outcome is indicated: the question remains open between a continuation of the decline and a possible turning point. ## How to read the signal for those who convert their salary
The useful data for someone who receives a salary in francs and converts it into euros is not an isolated percentage, but the sequence in which the analysis is presented. The text does not provide a euro amount for a single conversion: the 5% should therefore be read as a measure of the exchange-rate movement, not as an identical result for every salary. To make the comparison practical, [busta paga svizzera](nav:payslip) can be the starting point for determining the amount in francs to monitor.
| Reference | Reported data | |---|---| | Highs in the first part of 2026 | Starting point of the decline | | Movement after the spring 2026 peak | About 5% lower against the euro | | 2023 | Decline to similar levels | | 2024 | Correction of over 6% |
The historical comparison puts two opposite readings into perspective. On the one hand, the current decline is not described as an exceptional movement: declines of a similar magnitude have already appeared over the last five years. On the other hand, the fact that the correction has already reached about 5% does not prove that the decline is over.
### Three scenarios to distinguish
In the first scenario, weakness continues in the coming weeks. For someone converting their salary, the weaker franc continues to translate into fewer euros for the same salary. In the second, the decline loses momentum. This possibility is compatible with the observation that several periods of weakness in recent years began to slow in a similar area.
The third scenario is waiting. Statistical signals and institutional investors' positioning make the coming weeks relevant, but the source does not present these elements as a guarantee of a reversal. The practical point is to keep the historical data and the interpretation separate: the comparison with 2023 and 2024 helps interpret the movement, but does not by itself establish what the exchange rate's next step will be.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## Simple monitoring for the coming weeks
The question about the turning point is not resolved by a single data point. However, the analysis can be followed through a four-step process, using only the references indicated.
1. Use as a reference the highs reached in the first part of 2026 and the peak of spring 2026, after which the observed movement began.
2. Measure the distance from the previous highs and note the figure indicated by the analysis: the franc has lost approximately 5% against the euro. This percentage describes the exchange rate, not a personal conversion that has already been calculated.
3. Reconstruct the comparison with the last five years. 2023 offers a reference with similar decline levels; 2024 shows a correction that exceeded 6%. These are points of comparison, not targets to reach.
4. Follow the window between the end of September and the beginning of November. Seasonality was analyzed with Forecaster based on the franc’s average behavior over the last ten years, but the text signals only a particular dynamic and does not indicate a certain outcome.
During the regular conversion of your salary, it is advisable to maintain the same basis of observation: salary in francs, relationship with the euro, and distance from the indicated highs. In this way, the comparison remains readable even if the decline were to continue or begin to lose strength.
The caution concerns above all the low point. The analysis does not say that it has already been reached; it only maintains that a significant part of the downward movement could be behind us. item.title: More federal funds for integration 2028-2032
item.description: The Federal Council allocates 334.5 million for integration in Switzerland for the period 2028-2032, with 66.9 million annually for cantonal and national programmes.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - 334,5 million allocated for the 2028-2032 period - 66,9 million per year, 5,4 more than before - 37,3 million annually to the Cantons for integration - 29,6 million annually to national programmes
## Key facts - Decision: Federal Council - Period: 2028-2032 - Total credit: 334,5 million - Annual allocation: 66,9 million - Cantonal measures: 37,3 million annually - National programmes: 29,6 million annually - Employment rate of immigrants: 77%
On Friday, the Federal Council decided to increase support for promoting integration in Switzerland. For the 2028-2032 period, it allocated a credit of 334,5 million francs for cantonal integration programmes, referred to as PIC, and projects of national importance.
Every year, the Confederation will make 66,9 million francs available. This is 5,4 million more per year. The annual allocation is divided between the portion intended for the Cantons and that reserved for national programmes, according to the two lines set out in the federal decision.
### The priorities indicated
The Cantons will receive 37,3 million francs annually for measures to promote language skills, information, counselling and educational and professional integration. Their contribution must be at least equal to the federal contribution. The supported activities therefore include both language acquisition and pathways related to education and work.
The priorities include removing barriers to the integration of women and strengthening educational pathways. The stated aim is to promote labour market integration by linking integration to education and professional participation.
Another 29,6 million francs per year will finance national programmes, including the integration pre-apprenticeship. Finally, the source links the new funds to the results of the cantonal programmes, active since 2014: the employment rate of immigrants in Switzerland is 77%, among the highest in the OECD area. ## What changes for cantons and beneficiaries
On a practical level, the decision strengthens a structure in which the cantons have a direct role. The annual share of 37.3 million francs is allocated to four areas: language promotion, information, counselling and educational and professional integration. For those seeking an integration pathway, these categories help distinguish the type of measure to identify at cantonal level.
The comparison with the previous situation is given by the increase of 5.4 million francs per year. The Confederation will thus bring its annual allocation to 66.9 million. For cantonal measures, however, federal funding must be accompanied by a share from the cantons at least equivalent to it. The overall value of cantonal interventions therefore does not coincide with the federal amount alone.
### Two distinct channels
The announced allocation separates two channels. The first concerns cantonal integration programmes, or PICs, with resources for language, information, counselling, education and work. The second concerns national programmes, funded with 29.6 million per year and also including the integration pre-apprenticeship.
The distinction is also useful for understanding the priorities. A language difficulty falls under language promotion; a need for orientation under information or counselling. The transition towards education and professional integration, on the other hand, falls within the educational and professional pathways indicated by the Federal Council.
The priority dedicated to women signals that removing obstacles to integration is an explicit part of the new direction. Strengthening educational pathways aims to establish a connection with work. Those who want to complement this perspective with the search for professional opportunities can consult the [annunci di lavoro](nav:jobs), keeping the editorial tool and public funding separate.
The 77% figure for the employment rate of immigrants in Switzerland describes the results attributed to the cantonal programmes since 2014. It does not, however, constitute an automatic forecast for the 2028-2032 period: the decision indicates the objectives and resources, not a new expected employment rate.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ## How to navigate the measures
The first step is to identify the area of need. Measures funded through cantonal programmes concern language promotion, information, counselling, and educational and professional integration. These are the categories to use when reviewing initiatives linked to the PICs.
The second step is to distinguish the programme level. If the intervention falls under the PICs, the share indicated for the Cantons is 37,3 million francs per year and requires a cantonal contribution at least equal to the federal one. If, instead, it is a national initiative, the reference is the annual share of 29,6 million, which also includes the integration pre-apprenticeship.
### A practical framework
To follow implementation during the 2028-2032 period, it is advisable to look in your own Canton for measures falling under the four areas indicated. Those who need to strengthen their language skills can turn to language promotion; those who need guidance can consider information and counselling. For those aiming for education or work, the reference point is educational and professional pathways.
The priority given to women should be considered when the problem concerns specific obstacles to integration. item.title: Phytosanitary approval: backlog cleared by 2032
item.description: Federal Council sets 2032 to process 525 pending applications; fees increasing from 2028 to cover 50% of costs.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Federal Council sets 2032 as the deadline for pending applications - The backlog has fallen from more than 700 to around 525 - Authorisation fees will increase from 2028 - The plan provides for around 18 million francs by 2032
## Key facts - Date → 25 September 2026 - Location → Bern - Authorities involved → FSVO, FOEN, FOAG, SECO - Objective → all pending applications processed by 2032 - Supplementary credit 2027 → 2,8 million francs - Cost coverage → from 15% toward around 50% - Deadline for amending the ordinance → end of 2027
## Federal decision
In Bern, on 25 September 2026, the Federal Council decided that all pending authorisation applications for plant protection products should be processed within six years. The deadline indicated in the communication is 2032. The measure concerns a federal procedure that precedes market placement: every product must be authorised by the Confederation, which verifies its efficacy and the risks to humans and the environment.
The dossier directly concerns farmers, who need effective and safe products to protect crops from pests or fungal infestations. The assessments are scientific but complex. With limited staffing resources, the number of pending applications increased for several years, and waiting times particularly delayed the market placement of modern plant protection products.
### The authorities involved
At the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office, the Federal Office for the Environment FOEN, the Federal Office for Agriculture FOAG and the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs SECO, several hundred applications are pending. The Federal Administration has reduced the backlog from more than 700 to around 525 applications, but the Federal Council considers that the pace is still insufficient.
The decision provides for more staff resources, further digitisation of the procedure, better information for applicants on the status of their cases and fewer interfaces between offices. The aim is to make the process more efficient and customer-oriented, while also closing the gaps created when products are no longer available on the market for certain harmful organisms.
The plan provides for around 18 million francs by 2032 for the FSVO and FOAG: 16 million for the FSVO and 2 million for the FOAG. Funding is guaranteed through the ordinary budgeting process. For 2027, the two offices will submit a request for a supplementary credit of 2,8 million to Parliament. From 2028, the necessary resources will have to be offset by an increase in authorisation fees. The FDHA will have to submit an amendment to the ordinance on fees to the Federal Council by the end of 2027. ## Practical analysis: what changes
The practical value of the measure can be seen on two levels. For farmers, the problem described is not only the wait: emergency approvals are currently being granted for older products, while modern substitutes are still in the approval process. For some harmful organisms, no products are available anymore. Clearing the backlog is therefore linked to availability gaps, without guaranteeing the approval of a specific product.
### Four indicators to read together
| Aspect | Situation described | Decided direction | |---|---|---| | Applications | Over 700 → approximately 525; insufficient time | Processing by 2032 | | Products | Older products used in emergencies | Fill the gaps | | Costs | Coverage of approximately 15% | Toward approximately 50%; higher fees from 2028 | | Organization | Complex checks; limited staff | More staff and digitalization |
For anyone submitting an application, the clearest difference concerns funding. Current coverage is only approximately 15 per cent of costs; the Federal Council wants to bring it closer to approximately 50 per cent of the level for EU authorizations. The increase in fees is announced from 2028. The source does not indicate a fee per individual application: it is therefore not possible to calculate the amount payable by an applicant.
The financial schedule must be separated from the individual case. The approximately 18 million francs by 2032 concern investments at USAV and UFAG, while the 2,8 million for 2027 are a supplementary credit request that the two offices will submit to Parliament. Neither amount is indicated as a fee for a single application. For an overview of personal income, [calcolatore stipendio](nav:calculator) cannot turn these figures into an individual charge.
The organizational measures follow the same logic: more digitalization, fewer interfaces and better information on progress should make the process clearer for applicants. However, the release does not indicate a schedule for each case, nor the outcome of a single application. The 2032 objective concerns all pending applications. The text does not quantify any effect on [costo della vita in Svizzera](nav:cost-of-living) either.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [CHF-EUR exchange comparator](nav:exchange). ## How to follow the process
The source makes it possible to construct an operational sequence based on the deadlines indicated, but it does not describe forms, documents or a portal for applications. Therefore, the reader can follow the decision calendar without adding unannounced administrative steps.
### Five steps for applicants and operators
1. If an approval application is still pending, consider it part of the backlog that the Federal Council wants to clear by 2032. The communication does not indicate a ranking or an individual deadline.
2. For 2027, distinguish the request for supplementary credit from the approval procedure: USAV and UFAG will submit a total request of 2.8 million francs to Parliament.
3. By the end of 2027, follow the step planned for the DFI, which will have to submit the amendment to the ordinance on fees to the Federal Council. The proposal concerns the degree of cost coverage, currently around 15 per cent.
4. From 2028, take into account the increase in approval fees announced to offset the resources needed. The source does not specify the amount of the individual fee, so it does not allow for a more precise estimate.
5. Use 2032 as the horizon for the overall measure. As part of the process, the Federal Administration will have to strengthen staffing, further digitize the procedure, better inform applicants about the status of their applications and reduce interfaces between offices.
For farmers, the operational interpretation remains linked to product availability: the communication points out that for some harmful organisms there are no longer any products on the market and that emergency authorizations concern older products. item.title: Switzerland: new standalone cybersecurity law LCib
item.description: The Federal Council instructs DDPS to draft the LCib by June 2027, based on the European Cyber Resilience Act for digital products and data.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - DDPS will prepare a standalone cybersecurity law. - The draft will be ready by June 2027 for consultation. - The law will bring together three projects on products, data and digital infrastructure. - The obligation to report cyberattacks will be transferred from the LSIn to the LCib.
## Key facts - Decision → Federal Council, 25 September 2026 - Mandate → DDPS - Deadline → June 2027 - Planned law → standalone federal Cybersecurity Act (LCib) - Basis → European Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) - Areas → products, data and digital infrastructure - Obligation transferred → reporting of cyberattacks on critical infrastructure - LSIn → information security of the federal authorities
On 25 September 2026, at its meeting in Bern, the Federal Council instructed the Federal Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport (DDPS) to prepare by June 2027 a draft for consultation on a new standalone federal cybersecurity law. The stated objective is to implement three parliamentary initiatives in a single legislative act.
The Federal Office for Cyber Security (FOCS) is working on the projects on behalf of Parliament. The first concerns the cyber-resilience of products with digital elements; the second, the protection of the most important digital data; the third, the role of hosting and cloud service providers in cybersecurity. The three projects concern complementary regulatory levels: products, data and digital infrastructure. They were originally intended to be implemented through amendments to the Federal Act on Information Security (LSIn).
### The choice of a standalone law
The Federal Council is now changing its approach. The planned Cybersecurity Act, referred to as the LCib, will bring together the three projects and ensure coherent regulation of cybersecurity by third parties. The new act will also include the obligation to report cyberattacks on critical infrastructure, provided for by the LSIn and in force since April 2025. The LSIn, however, will continue to govern the information security of the federal authorities.
The draft will establish binding requirements for manufacturers, importers and distributors of software and hardware products. It will also create the basis for market surveillance and for a ban on distributing unsafe products. Special obligations are envisaged for important digital data and for hosting and cloud providers, including cooperation and defence in the event of cyberthreats.
The sector-specific rules already in force, including the Telecommunications Act, the Ordinance on the Electricity Supply and the Ordinance on Telecommunications Installations, will remain in force. The LCib will supplement them with cybersecurity obligations. According to the Federal Council, a single law will make it possible to update just one act based on technological or European developments and to address specific issues better, such as open-source software.
DDPS will have to submit the draft to the Federal Council by June 2027, for consultation and the subsequent decision. The planned legislation will be based on the European Cyber Resilience Act (CRA) and aims to keep companies' administrative burden to a minimum. For companies active internationally that already have to comply with the EU CRA, the stated objective is to avoid an additional compliance burden. ## What changes for organizations
The transition from three amendments to the LSIn to a standalone law introduces a simpler framework for the organizations involved: distinguishing the scope of the activity and placing each obligation under the applicable set of rules. The communiqué describes a project, not an entry-into-force date: the DDPS will have to draft it by June 2027, put it out for consultation and submit it to the Federal Council for a decision. The practical consequence is to keep the obligations already in force separate from those that the LCib will have to define.
| Scope | Measure described | Planned placement | |---|---|---| | Products with digital elements | Binding requirements, market surveillance and a ban on distributing unsafe products | LCib | | Important digital data | Specific protection obligations | LCib | | Hosting and cloud | Obligations to cooperate and defend against cyber threats | LCib | | Critical infrastructure | Reporting of cyberattacks in force since April 2025 | Planned transfer from the LSIn to the LCib | | Sector-specific rules | Laws and ordinances remain in force | Integration of cybersecurity obligations |
### A map by entity
For a manufacturer, importer or distributor, the dossier covers binding requirements, market surveillance and a possible ban on distributing unsafe products. For a hosting or cloud provider, the text instead focuses on cooperation and defense in the event of cyber threats. Important digital data form a further scope, with specific protection obligations.
The most explicit economic benefit concerns companies operating internationally. Since these companies already have to comply with the EU CRA, the harmonized Swiss law is designed not to create an additional compliance burden. The proposal should also keep companies' administrative burdens to a minimum. The reference to the European CRA thus becomes the main point of comparison for those operating across borders.
Sector-specific rules are neither absorbed nor repealed: the Telecommunications Act, the Ordinance on Electricity Supply and the Ordinance on Telecommunications Installations remain in force, while the LCib adds cybersecurity obligations as a joint task. For federal authorities, the LSIn continues to govern information security.
To explore the business perspective separately from the regulatory dossier, see [aziende che assumono](nav:companies).
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## How to follow the dossier
Following the dossier first of all requires separating the roles, because the project does not concern just one type of entity. The operational sequence can remain aligned with the areas listed in the communication.
### Five operational steps
1. **Map the scope.** Verify whether the activity concerns the production, import or distribution of software and hardware with digital elements, the protection of important digital data, hosting or cloud services, or critical infrastructure. These are the four areas for which the text provides for specific measures.
2. Separate the rules that already apply from the project. For critical infrastructures, bear in mind the obligation to report cyberattacks in force since April 2025. Its planned placement will be in the LCib; it should not be confused with the part of the LSIn that will continue to regulate the information security of federal authorities.
3. Maintain the sectoral framework. The Telecommunications Act, the Ordinance on the Electricity Supply and the Ordinance on Telecommunications Installations will remain in force. The new law will supplement them by adding the obligations arising from cybersecurity as a joint task.
4. Distinguish products and services. For products, follow the binding requirements, market surveillance and the possible distribution ban on unsafe products. For hosting and cloud, instead separate out the planned obligations of cooperation and defence in the event of cyber threats.
5. Note the legislative deadline. By June 2027, DDPS will have to prepare the project, submit it for consultation and submit it to the Federal Council for a decision. For companies active internationally, the European CRA constitutes the reference indicated for future Swiss legislation.
This timetable makes it possible not to anticipate an application date that the communication does not indicate. The certain step is the preparation of the project and its subsequent consultation; the Federal Council will then have to receive it for a decision. For companies, the practical question is therefore which of the scopes affects their activity and how it intersects with sectoral rules or with the CRA already applied by companies active internationally. The standalone law is also intended to update a single act based on technological or European developments and to address specific topics more effectively, such as open-source software.
Those following the issue professionally can also consult the [annunci di lavoro](nav:jobs), keeping this tool separate from the legislative process. To instead connect the reading to your personal situation, use the [calcolatore stipendio](nav:calculator).

item.title: LSD: end of bovine vaccination on September 30, 2026
item.description: The campaign ends on 30/09/2026. An 8-month wait with targeted surveillance until June 2027 begins on October 1.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Mandatory vaccination until September 30, 2026 - Eight-month waiting period starting October 1, 2026 - Targeted surveillance from January 2027 - Disease-free status not before June 1, 2027
## Key facts - Publication → September 24, 2026 - End of vaccination → September 30, 2026 - Start of waiting period → October 1, 2026 - Targeted surveillance → January 2027 - Disease-free country status → not before June 1, 2027
### The decision and the timeline
The press release published on September 24, 2026, announces that the mandatory vaccination campaign against Contagious Capripoxvirus (Lumpy Skin Disease) in cattle will end on September 30, 2026, in the Canton of Geneva and in the vaccination zones of the Cantons of Vaud and Valais. Starting October 1, 2026, an eight-month waiting period will begin.
During the waiting period, cantonal veterinary services will maintain enhanced surveillance for any signs attributable to LSD, under the coordination of the Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO). Specific rules regarding animal movements will continue to apply. If surveillance results and the evolution of the epizootic situation in Europe remain favorable, Switzerland may regain its LSD disease-free country status not before June 1, 2027.
This measure responds to a situation observed across the border. Since June 2025, outbreaks have occurred in Italy and France; several French outbreaks were identified less than 50 kilometers from the Swiss border. To protect Swiss cattle herds and prevent the introduction of the virus, Switzerland established vaccination zones in the Canton of Geneva and in certain areas of the Cantons of Vaud and Valais. In these zones, several thousand animals have already been vaccinated, while to date, no confirmed case of LSD has been recorded in Switzerland.
For the 2026 season, the FSVO has also prohibited the summer grazing of cattle in France. Mandatory vaccination continues until September 30 in the affected areas to protect animals born in those zones or introduced during the period of biting insect activity. The favorable development makes it possible for the vaccination obligation to lapse on that date, but the interruption does not end the control measures: from October 1, the territories will retain their status as vaccination zones and the amendments to the FSVO ordinance will enter into force.
From January 2027, targeted surveillance will begin in the vaccination zones of the three Cantons, with the aim of confirming the absence of virus circulation in Switzerland. The specific arrangements will be communicated to animal keepers in due course, and surveillance will be adapted to the evolution of the epizootic situation. ## Animal movements: the transition from 1 October
### Easier entry, exits still conditional
The most visible operational change concerns animal traffic. From 1 October 2026, animals originating from territories outside the vaccination zones of the Cantons of Geneva, Vaud and Valais will be able to access those zones without having to be vaccinated after arrival. Access is thus facilitated, while the maintenance of vaccination zone status shows that the end of the obligation does not coincide with the immediate removal of precautions.
For exits, the requirement depends on the animal's protection. The source distinguishes between unvaccinated calves protected by antibodies transmitted from the vaccinated mother, unvaccinated animals or non-immunised calves, and vaccinated animals.
| Situation | Condition from 1 October 2026 | |---|---| | Entry from territories outside the zone | No vaccination after arrival | | Unvaccinated calf, protected by maternal antibodies | Clinical examination | | Unvaccinated animal or non-immunised calf | Negative virus or antibody test and clinical examination at the farm of origin | | Vaccinated animal | Transfer inside or outside zones if all animals of the farm of origin have undergone a clinical examination |
This distinction makes the clinical examination the common point of several pathways. For a calf protected by maternal antibodies, the clinical examination allows exit. For an unvaccinated animal or a non-immunised calf, a negative screening test for the virus or for antibodies is also required, in addition to the clinical examination at the farm of origin. For vaccinated animals transferred inside or outside the zones, the indicated condition is that all animals of the farm of origin have been subjected to a clinical examination.
The comparison between entry and exit is therefore clear-cut. An external animal can enter without vaccination after arrival, but the exiting categories must comply with different conditions. Zones and restrictions may be lifted no earlier than 1 June 2027 if surveillance and the epizootic situation in Europe remain favourable. Until then, movements require attention to the condition applicable to each individual category.
The health framework explains the caution. LSD affects cattle, buffaloes and bison; it is transmitted mainly through bites of blood-feeding flies and mosquitoes and presents characteristic symptoms such as fever, lethargy and skin nodules. It is not transmissible to humans. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare [CHF-EUR exchange options](nav:exchange) and [banks for cross-border workers](nav:banks). ## Cosa devono fare i detentori
### Una sequenza operativa fino a giugno 2027
Per i detentori di animali, il periodo di attesa richiede una routine precisa. La fonte indica una sequenza pratica: sorvegliare, segnalare i sospetti e applicare la condizione corretta prima di ogni movimento.
1. Dal 1 ottobre 2026, osservare attentamente i propri animali. Febbre, spossatezza e noduli sulla pelle sono i segni caratteristici da riconoscere.
2. Se compare un sospetto, notificare immediatamente il veterinario. I campioni saranno prelevati e inviati in laboratorio per l'analisi.
3. Per l'accesso alle zone, identificare la provenienza: gli animali da territori esterni possono entrare senza dover essere vaccinati dopo l'arrivo.
4. Per l'uscita, controllare la categoria. Un vitello non vaccinato ma protetto dagli anticorpi della madre vaccinata può uscire dopo un esame clinico. Per un animale non vaccinato o un vitello non immunizzato servono un test di screening negativo per il virus o per gli anticorpi e un esame clinico nell'azienda di provenienza. Gli animali vaccinati possono essere trasferiti dentro o fuori dalle zone se tutti gli animali dell'azienda da cui provengono hanno sostenuto un esame clinico.
5. Da gennaio 2027, seguire le indicazioni sulla sorveglianza mirata nelle zone di Ginevra, Vaud e Vallese. Le modalità saranno comunicate a tempo debito e potranno adattarsi alla situazione epizootica.
Restano valide le raccomandazioni di biosicurezza e protezione dagli insetti. L'USAV continuerà a seguire la situazione in Svizzera e all'estero e adeguerà le misure se necessario. La fine dell'obbligo vaccinale non coincide con la revoca immediata delle zone: in caso di risultati favorevoli, zone e restrizioni potranno essere revocate non prima del 1 giugno 2027 e la Svizzera potrà riottenere lo status di Paese indenne da LSD.
Nel frattempo, ogni decisione di spostamento va collegata alla posizione dell'azienda, allo stato vaccinale o immunitario dell'animale e all'esito degli esami richiesti. Il comunicato mantiene questa distinzione fino alla nuova valutazione della situazione.

item.title: Made in Europe: Switzerland seeks place in EU procurement
item.description: On 24 September 2026 in Brussels, the inclusion of Switzerland in the EU industrial acceleration law was discussed, with Germany in favour and France against.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Germany opens to Switzerland in the «Made in Europe» initiative - France wants public funds only for EU industry - Poland still considers Swiss inclusion open - The issue is discussed in Brussels on 24 September 2026
## Key facts - What: industrial acceleration law - Objective: «European preference» in public procurement - Germany: «Made with Europe» approach - France: public funds for industries of the 27 EU Member States - Poland: possible different criterion per sector - Spain: initial group of the 27 EU Member States
On 24 September 2026 in Brussels, the possibility of including Switzerland was discussed in the European debate on the future «Made in Europe» initiative. German Economy Minister Katherina Reiche asked to include trade partners such as Switzerland; French Industry Minister Sébastien Martin argued instead that public funds should go only to industries of the EU Member States.
The discussion took place as the two ministers arrived at the Competitiveness Council, a meeting attended by the competent ministers of the 27 EU Member States. On the table was strengthening European industry. The concept of «Made in Europe» falls under the industrial acceleration law proposed by the European Commission in spring.
### European preference in procurement
The proposal aims to introduce a «European preference» in public procurement for certain industrial sectors. The still controversial point is the definition of «European»: it remains to be established whether and to what extent third countries such as Switzerland can fall under this setting.
Reiche spoke of «Made with Europe» and indicated production in Europe together with trade partners, citing Norway, Switzerland and Canada. Martin replied that in «Made in Europe» there is «Europe», referring to the 27 EU States. He clarified that the proposal does not foresee tariffs and that the priority is an agreement among the 27; Switzerland, he added, does not sit in the Council.
Poland and Spain also left various possibilities open. Polish Secretary of State for the Economy Michal Baranowski said it is too early to decide whether Switzerland will be included, pointing to the involvement of key partners and different rules for product categories, provided they are simple. Spanish Industry Minister Jordi Hereu first indicated the group of the 27, then a possible enlarged group with the EEA States and consolidated partners, among which Switzerland could be included. A third group would comprise countries with free‑trade agreements or other specific accords.
Swiss economic associations and the Confederation are closely following the negotiations. In early September, a high‑level economic delegation travelled to Brussels. ...

item.title: Salasso at the pump: expensive diesel, gasoline on the rise
item.description: On 24 September 2026 in Zurich diesel costs on average 2.46 CHF/l (peaks >2.50), petrol 95 2.14 CHF/l, while oil exceeds 100 USD/barrel.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Diesel reaches an average of 2.46 francs per liter. - Unleaded 95 is at a median of 2.14 francs. - Refineries are shifting production towards diesel. - Goldman Sachs sees increases for gasoline in mid-2027. ## Key facts - Date → September 24, 2026 - Location → Zurich - Diesel → average of 2.46 francs per liter - Peaks → over 2.50 francs per liter - Gasoline → unleaded 95 at a median of 2.14 francs - Oil → over 100 dollars per barrel - Outlook → rise in European gasoline for mid-2027. ### The gap at the pump On September 24, 2026, in Zurich, the Swiss fuel market shows an already heavy gap. Those who own a gasoline car have so far had only relative relief: the increase has occurred, but the price of unleaded 95 remains lower than diesel. According to the TCS fuel radar, diesel in Switzerland has reached an average of 2.46 francs per liter, with peaks over 2.50. Unleaded 95 instead moves along the median, still high, of 2.14 francs. For those who drive a car, the comparison shows how the advantage of gasoline is still visible today, but already within an inflated market. That advantage could, however, disappear soon. It is the outlook reported by Blick in a recent article on expensive fuel in Switzerland, after the alarm contained in a Goldman Sachs report picked up by Bloomberg. The thesis concerns production: today diesel yields more and refineries are shifting production from gasoline to diesel. If the amount of gasoline in circulation decreases, its price can rise. The logic indicated by analysts is that of supply: less product available means greater pressure on prices. Diesel could continue to rise, but gasoline now has more room for an increase. For this reason, the investment bank advises investors to bet on an increase in European gasoline for mid-2027. The forecast concerns European gasoline and places the possibility of an increase in the middle of next year. In Switzerland, the risk is recognized by industry insiders. Olivier Fantino, director of Avenergy Suisse, the association of distributors that includes, among others, Agrola, Migrol, Socar and Tamoil, links the lack of refining capacity to a further increase in costs. The problem is structural: numerous refineries have been closed in Europe in recent years; in Russia and the Middle East, several plants have been damaged or destroyed by military actions. So far the shortage has mainly affected diesel, which has grown more than gasoline. For those living in Switzerland, the shift from a price difference to a possible increase in unleaded 95 translates into an item to monitor in the personal budget. The [cost of living in Switzerland](nav:cost-of-living) provides a tool to frame this expense together with other outgoings. ...
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). ### Una routine di controllo in quattro passaggi Per affrontare un possibile rincaro senza affidarsi a una cifra futura non ancora disponibile, conviene impostare una piccola routine di controllo. Non richiede una previsione personale: serve a distinguere i dati osservati dalle ipotesi degli analisti e a riportare nel bilancio solo ciò che si è effettivamente pagato.
1. Parti dal radar carburante del TCS. Annota il valore di riferimento per il carburante utilizzato, mantenendo separati diesel e senza piombo 95. In questo modo il confronto resta ancorato ai dati indicati per la Svizzera.
2. Registra la spesa reale. Conserva per ogni rifornimento la data, il tipo di carburante, il prezzo in franchi al litro e l'importo complessivo. La tabella personale consente di distinguere il prezzo effettivamente sostenuto dalla mediana nazionale.
3. Separa il dato dalla previsione. Tieni su una riga distinta i segnali provenienti dal rapporto di Goldman Sachs ripreso da Bloomberg e le valutazioni degli esperti. Un possibile aumento della benzina europea non va trattato come una quotazione già applicata a ogni distributore svizzero.
4. Controlla i fattori esterni indicati nella fonte. Gli sviluppi della guerra in Iran e di quella in Ucraina incidono sul petrolio; il livello del Reno riguarda il trasporto del carburante importato; l'ipotesi di Donald Trump riguarda l'export statunitense di diesel. Sono elementi diversi e vanno annotati separatamente.
Il passaggio successivo è aggiornare il bilancio con la spesa osservata, senza sostituirla con un aumento ipotetico. Se il costo del rifornimento cambia, la registrazione mostra subito quale voce si è modificata. Se resta stabile, la previsione degli analisti rimane un segnale da seguire, non un esborso già sostenuto.
Poiché la fonte segnala poche speranze di schiarite in tempi brevi, una verifica periodica è più utile di una decisione basata su un solo giorno. Il confronto tra radar TCS, spesa personale e aggiornamenti sul petrolio permette di mantenere distinta la situazione corrente dagli scenari futuri.

item.content:encoded:
## In breve - BNS: tasso guida fermo allo 0% dal giugno 2025 - Inflazione ad agosto allo 0,8%, spinta dall'energia - Crescita 2026 attesa tra 1,5% e 2%
## Fatti chiave - Decisione → politica monetaria invariata - Tasso guida → 0% - Inflazione agosto → 0,8% - Crescita 2026 → 1,5%-2% - Crescita 2027 → circa 1,5%
Il tasso guida della Banca nazionale svizzera resta allo 0%. La decisione, ampiamente attesa, lascia invariata la politica monetaria e conferma il livello a cui il tasso si trova dal giugno 2025. La notizia è stata diffusa con un comunicato ripreso da Keystone-ATS.
Anche la remunerazione degli averi a vista detenuti dalle banche presso la BNS non cambia. Fino a un determinato limite, gli averi continueranno a essere remunerati in base al tasso guida; per gli importi eccedenti quel limite resterà immutato il livello di 0,25 punti percentuali indicato nel comunicato.
### Prezzi e previsione inflazionistica
Da giugno l'inflazione è ulteriormente cresciuta e in agosto era allo 0,8%. La BNS collega principalmente il movimento al rincaro dell'energia. Nel medio termine, tuttavia, la pressione inflazionistica è aumentata solo di poco. L'istituto considera quindi appropriata la politica monetaria per mantenere l'inflazione nell'area di stabilità dei prezzi e sostenere l'andamento dell'economia.
La previsione condizionata indica un ulteriore aumento dell'inflazione nel quarto trimestre, seguito da una flessione nel corso del 2027. Secondo la BNS, il rincaro energetico, attualmente molto elevato, dovrebbe rallentare nei prossimi trimestri.
| Anno | Previsione BNS | Previsione precedente | |---|---:|---:| | 2026 | 0,7% | 0,6% a giugno | | 2027 | 0,8% | 0,6% | | 2028 | 0,8% | 0,7% |
La previsione assume che il tasso guida BNS resti pari allo 0% lungo l'intero orizzonte previsivo.
### Scenario mondiale e crescita svizzera
Nel suo scenario di base, la BNS prevede una crescita mondiale moderata nei prossimi trimestri, ma segnala un'elevata incertezza legata soprattutto alla situazione in Medio Oriente. Prezzi dell'energia nettamente superiori alle attese spingerebbero ancora l'inflazione e rallenterebbero sensibilmente la crescita economica. Anche il quadro della politica commerciale internazionale resta incerto.
Per la Svizzera, l'istituto prevede una crescita moderata, sostenuta dagli impulsi positivi dell'economia mondiale, dalla politica monetaria e dal deprezzamento del franco. Per l'intero 2026 la stima è ora compresa fra l'1,5% e il 2%, contro l'1% circa atteso tre mesi fa. Per il 2027 resta una previsione di crescita di circa l'1,5%. ....

## In breve - Gli Stati approvano la mozione con 24 voti a 18 - Tre astensioni accompagnano il voto - Il Consiglio federale dovrà preparare una base legale - La proposta riguarda costi di intervento e sicurezza

## Il voto a Berna
A Berna, il Consiglio degli Stati ha approvato con 24 voti contro 18 e 3 astensioni una mozione che apre alla possibilità di addebitare agli organizzatori i costi provocati da gravi disordini e atti violenti durante le manifestazioni. Il Nazionale si era già espresso favorevolmente; il passaggio agli Stati completa dunque il sostegno parlamentare alla richiesta, che ora passa al Consiglio federale per il lavoro legislativo indicato nel testo.
La mozione incarica il Consiglio federale di elaborare una base legale. L'obiettivo è permettere alle collettività pubbliche di riscuotere dagli organizzatori di proteste e dimostrazioni l'integralità o una parte dei costi dell'intervento e delle misure necessarie a garantirne la sicurezza. La fonte non descrive ancora una procedura di riscossione, né indica importi o una data di applicazione: il passaggio annunciato è la preparazione della base legale.
### Perché la proposta è arrivata in Parlamento
Il testo è stato depositato dal consigliere nazionale Sidney Kamerzin (Centro/VS). La motivazione richiama diverse manifestazioni recenti, in particolare quella dell'11 ottobre scorso a Berna, sfociate in violenze contro la popolazione per mano di estremisti violenti. Secondo la mozione, la prevenzione e la protezione hanno reso necessarie importanti misure delle forze dell'ordine.
Daniel Jositsch (Indipendente/ZH) ha sostenuto la richiesta affermando: «Non spetta alla collettività farsi carico dei costi legati a queste misure di sicurezza». Nel suo intervento ha citato anche una situazione di impunità che, ha detto, aveva constatato personalmente nelle vie di Zurigo.
Il voto non ha chiuso il confronto istituzionale. Carlo Sommaruga (PS/GE) ha contestato la mozione per il possibile contrasto con il principio di sussidiarietà e per i limiti che potrebbe imporre all'autonomia dei Cantoni. Mathias Zopfi (Verdi/GL) ha aggiunto che il testo è formulato in termini troppo ampi e potrebbe riguardare tutte le manifestazioni, comprese quelle del Primo maggio. Beat Jans, ministro della giustizia, ha ribadito la stessa obiezione. Il voto degli Stati riguarda quindi il mandato al Consiglio federale, non una cifra già stabilita per singoli eventi. ...

item.title: Interim: weather allowance after six months
item.description: The National Council approves the protection of temporary workers employed for at least six months in continuous relationships against interruptions due to bad weather.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The National Council approves the motion on temporary workers - The threshold is set at at least six months - The Council of States had amended the text - The act passes to the government for implementation
## Key facts - Decision → National Council - Requirement → at least six months - Relation → continuous employment - Process → transmission to the government
### The parliamentary decision
The National Council approved the motion of its own Social Security and Health Committee, already amended by the Council of States. The move concerns the current exclusion of the temporary work sector from bad‑weather allowances: temporary workers employed for at least six months in continuous employment relationships should no longer remain outside the scope envisaged by the text.
According to the promoting committee, the exclusion is not justified either by considerations relating to workers’ social security or by the intention to avoid dismissals. The motivation put before Parliament therefore concerns the treatment of temporary workers vis‑à‑vis interruptions of activity caused by bad weather.
The crux of the discussion was introduced by the Council of States during the examination of the motion, which took place last June. Senators deemed it appropriate to better protect long‑term temporary workers from work interruptions due to weather conditions. For this reason they narrowed the application of the text to continuous relationships with at least six months of employment.
The National Council, returning to the parliamentary act, followed the opinion of the Council of States. Thomas Rechsteiner (Centre/AI), speaking on behalf of the committee, indicated the temporal threshold as the point of balance of the amendment:
> «il limite di sei mesi crea una chiara distinzione tra incarichi di breve durata e rapporti di lavoro più stabili»
In the reasoning given in the chamber, short‑term engagements are characterised by greater flexibility. Weather‑related interruptions can, in part, be compensated by other assignments; for this reason, the entitlement to the allowance is not extended in a blanket manner to the whole temporary‑work sector. The approved protection is therefore linked to the duration and continuity of the relationship, not merely to belonging to the sector.
With the vote of the People’s Chamber, the parliamentary process described by the source completes the decisive step. The parliamentary act has been transmitted to the government, which must implement it. The news therefore concerns a decision approved by the National Council and an implementation entrusted to the subsequent governmental phase. The criterion chosen by the States and accepted by the National Council creates two distinct perimeters. The decision does not treat every temporary assignment in the same way: it links protection to the combination of two elements indicated in the text, at least six months of employment and a continuous employment relationship.
### Two different situations
| Situation | Expected effect according to the text | |---|---| | Continuous temporary relationship of at least six months | The worker is no longer excluded from the bad‑weather allowance after the act is implemented. | | Short‑term assignment | The extension does not become general for the whole sector. |
The before‑after comparison must be read with caution. Before the parliamentary intervention, the temporary‑work sector was excluded from this allowance. After the implementation of the decision, the change will concern the part of the sector defined by the six‑month requirement and continuity. Conversely, the text does not show an automatic extension to every temporary worker.
For an agency worker with a continuous relationship that reaches at least six months, the threshold becomes the central reference to understand whether their situation will fall within the foreseen protection. For those who carry out short assignments, the logic is different: greater flexibility and the possibility of partially compensating weather‑related interruptions with other assignments are the reason given for not extending the right in a generalised way.
This distinction also has a practical effect when reading job offers and employment relationships. A short assignment and a more stable relationship are no longer considered, in the approved text, as equivalent situations in the face of weather‑related interruptions. The decisive factor is not only that the work is temporary, but the indicated duration and the continuity of the relationship.
To orient themselves, anyone evaluating new [job postings](nav:jobs) must therefore separate the description of a short assignment from the situation of a worker employed long‑term. However, the link with the allowance is not yet an operational procedure defined in the described text: the act has been transmitted to the government, which will have to implement it. The parliamentary decision sets the criterion; its concrete implementation belongs to the next step.
The point remains as explained by the committee: better protect those who work long‑term, maintaining a distinction from short assignments. It is a selective choice, designed not to turn the allowance into a generalised right for the entire temporary‑work sector.

Per il lettore, la decisione può essere trasformata in una verifica in cinque passaggi, senza attribuire al testo informazioni che non contiene.
### Checklist di lettura
1. Individuare il tipo di rapporto. La misura riguarda il settore del lavoro temporaneo; il primo elemento da riconoscere è quindi se la propria situazione rientra in quel settore.
2. Controllare la durata indicata. Il requisito fissato dal testo è un impiego di almeno sei mesi. La soglia non va sostituita con una valutazione generica del fatto che l'incarico sembri lungo: è il limite temporale scelto nel passaggio parlamentare.
3. Verificare la continuità. I sei mesi devono riferirsi, secondo la modifica approvata, a rapporti di lavoro continuativi. La fonte precisa questo requisito, quindi la sola indicazione di un incarico temporaneo non descrive da sola il perimetro della modifica.
4. Separare l'evento considerato. La protezione riguarda le interruzioni del lavoro dovute alle intemperie o alle condizioni meteorologiche. Questo è il caso trattato dalla mozione; il testo non presenta una disciplina generale per ogni possibile interruzione.
5. Distinguere approvazione e attuazione. Il Consiglio nazionale ha seguito il parere degli Stati, ma l'atto parlamentare è stato trasmesso al governo, che dovrà attuarlo. La verifica personale deve quindi tenere separati il criterio già approvato e le modalità applicative che deriveranno dall'attuazione.
Questa checklist non può indicare un modulo, un ufficio, un importo o una scadenza, perché tali elementi non sono riportati nella fonte. Non è quindi corretto presentare la decisione come una procedura già completa. Il dato operativo disponibile è il perimetro: almeno sei mesi, rapporto continuativo, interruzione dovuta al maltempo, attuazione affidata al governo.
Chi vuole organizzare le informazioni sul proprio rapporto può usare la guida alla [busta paga svizzera](nav:payslip) come strumento editoriale del sito, senza confonderla con l'atto parlamentare. La questione dell'indennità resta legata al testo approvato e al successivo intervento governativo.
